issues.description: The UML class in the problem statement is declared as 'Course' (problem_statement.md) while the provided template and the solution both declare the class as 'Lecture' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). This naming mismatch (Course vs Lecture) can confuse students about which class they must implement and how to map the UML attributes/methods to the provided Java file.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts. Update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare 'class Lecture' (and adjust any labels that mention 'Course') so it matches the template and solution. If the intention was to use 'Course', rename the Java class files and all textual references to 'Course' consistently instead. Ensure the UML attribute names remain unchanged and still match the fields in Lecture.java.
